## Stages

Order follows the partner's ranking (O1 → O3). Hardening stages come after the three outcome stages. Each outcome stage needs only the previous one's real output, not its hardening.

- [ ] Stage 1: Filing-index table from real index files
      Objective: Build one filing-index table from real SEC quarterly and daily master index files.
      Outcomes: O1
      Consumes: nothing; package scaffolds only
      Produces: a queryable filing-index table with each row's archive path; specs/sec-filing-ingestion-stage-1-findings.md
      Exit: the table holds the rows of at least one real quarterly index and one quarter's real daily indexes, queryable by CIK, form type and filing date. The findings record files fetched, bytes, rows and wall time of the real run.
      Leaves out: full-history backfill (Stage 4); manifests and versioned publication (Stage 4); provenance (Stage 4); replay from raw bytes (Stage 4); reconciliation of later quarterly changes (Stage 5); shared SEC request budget (Stage 6); full validation suite (Stage 7); scheduling and deployment (Stage 8)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 2: Submissions download for a real sample
      Objective: Download the submissions that Stage 1's index rows name, for a bounded real range.
      Outcomes: O2
      Consumes: Stage 1's filing-index table and archive paths
      Produces: submissions on disk, each found from its index row's archive path; specs/sec-filing-ingestion-stage-2-findings.md
      Exit: every submission named by the index rows of one real quarter (or a sample the stage's spec bounds) is on disk, or is listed as failed. The findings record files, bytes, wall time and observed request rate, plus the full-history estimate derived from them.
      Leaves out: resumable bulk download (Stage 6); full-history submission download (Stage 6); shared SEC request budget (Stage 6); submission provenance (Stage 6); full validation suite (Stage 7); scheduling and deployment (Stage 8)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 3: 10-K and 8-K handling on the downloaded sample
      Objective: Pick 10-K and 8-K filings out of Stage 2's submissions and extract each one's main document.
      Outcomes: O3
      Consumes: Stage 2's submissions on disk; Stage 1's form types
      Produces: an extracted main document per 10-K and 8-K in the sample; specs/sec-filing-ingestion-stage-3-findings.md
      Exit: each 10-K and 8-K in Stage 2's sample has its main document extracted to a readable file, or is listed with its failure reason. The findings record counts, failures and time per filing.
      Leaves out: extraction over the full submission history (Stage 6); full validation suite (Stage 7); scheduling and deployment (Stage 8)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 4: Index catalog at full history
      Objective: Extend the filing-index table to the full history with daily catch-up, adding the four qualities Stage 1 left out.
      Outcomes: O1
      Consumes: Stage 1's table and findings
      Produces: a full-history filing-index catalog that readers resolve through a manifest; raw index bytes retained
      Exit: these four observable results.
        - full-history backfill: the catalog covers every requested quarter through the present, and unresolved gaps are listed.
        - manifests and versioned publication: readers reach the current version only through its manifest.
        - provenance: each row names its source file and hash.
        - replay from raw bytes: a parser change rebuilds the catalog with zero SEC requests.
      Leaves out: reconciliation of later quarterly changes (Stage 5); shared SEC request budget (Stage 6); full validation suite (Stage 7); scheduling and deployment (Stage 8)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 5: Reconciliation of later quarterly changes
      Objective: Re-read quarterly indexes and account for later SEC changes without discarding earlier versions.
      Outcomes: O1
      Consumes: Stage 4's manifests and versioned publication, provenance and retained raw bytes
      Produces: reconciliation of later quarterly changes, with prior catalog versions readable
      Exit: a re-read quarterly index records each addition, changed field and withdrawal against the prior version. The prior version stays readable.
      Leaves out: full validation suite (Stage 7); scheduling and deployment (Stage 8)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 6: Submissions and extraction at scale
      Objective: Take submission download and 10-K/8-K extraction to the full requested history under one SEC request budget.
      Outcomes: O2, O3
      Consumes: Stage 2 and Stage 3 findings; Stage 4's catalog
      Produces: four qualities for submissions and extraction: resumable bulk download, full-history submission download, a shared SEC request budget and submission provenance. It also produces extraction over the full submission history.
      Exit: these five observable results.
        - resumable bulk download: an interrupted download resumes without re-fetching completed files.
        - full-history submission download: the requested range is on disk, with gaps listed.
        - shared SEC request budget: index and submission collectors running together stay under the configured request rate in a measured run.
        - submission provenance: each submission names its index row and hash.
        - extraction over the full submission history: every 10-K and 8-K in range is extracted or listed as failed.
      Leaves out: full validation suite (Stage 7); scheduling and deployment (Stage 8)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 7: Full validation suite
      Objective: Cover the index, submission and extraction paths with an offline test suite.
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O3
      Consumes: Stages 1–6 as shipped
      Produces: full validation suite in CI
      Exit: CI runs with no SEC network access, over committed fixtures. The fixtures cover the historical index formats in range, malformed and HTML-error responses, which fail closed, and 10-K/8-K extraction cases.
      Leaves out: scheduling and deployment (Stage 8)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 8: Scheduling and deployment
      Objective: Run ongoing ingestion on a schedule in a deployed environment.
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O3
      Consumes: Stages 4–7
      Produces: scheduling and deployment, with monitoring and runbooks
      Exit: daily index ingestion runs on its schedule in the deployed environment, catches up after a missed run, and alerts on failure. Runbooks cover recovery.
      Leaves out: nothing
      ROUTING: brainstorming
